page0.text:
The sun is setting, and the lobby slowly wrapped in darkness.
...We came to the castle to find an ally, but the only thing remaining is the ruins of a castle after a turn of events.

page1.text:
"So, what should we do? I think we can stay here and strengthen our defense, without attacking.
We have food and can stay warm here. If we fix the walls, we can manage to protect ourselves in the castle."

page2.text:
...
That's the best thing to do if we want to protect ourselves.
But we even gained an ally to choose the path to fight because we couldn't do so.

page3.text:
"...No, it would be meaningless even if we strengthened our defense.
Any defense would be broken once Caster completely controls Saber.
...Even if we do survive here, if the Holy Grail becomes Caster's, then..."

page4.text:
"Not only us, but the people in town will suffer as well.
...Then there's only one thing to do. We'll get Saber back before Caster fully controls her. We have to defeat Caster, Archer, Assassin, and Mr. Kuzuki by ourselves."

page5.text:
...
I nod silently.
Since we couldn't get the help of Illya, we have to do this by ourselves.
...The sun will completely set soon.
We'll have to get out of this place before that and attack Caster before Saber surrenders...

page6.text:
It's a simple plan.
The process will change depending on the situation. Our only objective is to confront Caster as a result.

page7.text:
It doesn't matter whether that situation is only for an instant.
Caster is the weakest Servant when it comes to hand-to-hand combat.
Even if she may be a Servant, we have a chance at winning if we can fight her two against one.
Tohsaka's gems and my Projection magecraft.
It's not a battle we can't win if we make full use of our individual powers.

page8.text:
That was the conclusion that we reached, and we go out of the forest believing in that.
We don't exchange words after that.
...There's one reason.
We're desperately bluffing so that we can deceive ourselves.

page9.text:
The sunrise is gray.
The sunlight is blocked by the clouds, obscuring the light of dawn.
A cloudy sky is above us.
The sky that is closer to gray than black reminds me of that time ten years ago.

page10.text:
Is it going to start raining soon?
A dull white sky.
That man was standing under the cloudy sky that smelled like it had just stopped raining.

page11.text:
"So you did come. I know your personality. I thought you would come back with some kind of strategy."
He stares at Tohsaka with cool eyes.

page12.text:
"I'm sorry, Archer. I can't live up to those expectations.
As you can see, we're empty-handed. We brainstormed a whole day, but we couldn't come up with any plan."

page13.text:
"...What?"
"You might not believe me, but we came here to die an honorable death.
...But, it looks like we have a bit of luck left. If you're here, that means Saber is still going against Caster."

page14.text:
Then, there are four opponents.
If we break through Archer, the gatekeeper, we can fight Caster and Assassin head-on.
Our plan is that we break through Archer together and confront Caster with the two of us.
...That's the lie Tohsaka made up.

page15.text:
"...I see. Caster and Shirou Emiya. The scale tipped to Caster, huh, Rin?"
Archer's oppressive question.

page16.text:
"Yes. I hate my own personality, but I guess I can't change it since I'm born with it. I'm inhuman when it counts most after all."
Tohsaka answers with an emotionless voice and steps forward.

page17.text:
"...Shirou. Archer will only attack you. I won't back you up. I'll fight Caster while you get killed."
As if that's a crime...
Tohsaka apologizes with her back, as if she was intending to use me as a sacrifice from the start.

page18.text:
...
How stupid of her.
She didn't have to say such a thing.

page19.text:
"Don't worry about it, idiot. I also know your personality."
"Huh...?"
"Tohsaka, it's your principle not to do anything that you don't have a chance of winning at, right? That's why I knew. ...This is certainly the only way we can win."

page20.text:
"...Shirou."
Her back that didn't have any hesitation shakes slightly.
...Oh.
That's all the apology I need.

page21.text:
"Go. I'll hold Archer down. I'll hold him down, even if it's with will, at least until you get inside the church."
I control my breathing and turn the gears of my engine.
My condition is better than ever.
I can project the same swords as him right away in this state.

page22.text:
"...Thanks. Sorry, Shirou."
Tohsaka runs.
...Archer lets her go as if she was not in his sight from the start.
"Well done. It seems like you understand your powers, even while being incompetent."
He emits the intent to kill, as if to say he won't let me go this time.

page23.text:
"Trace, on."
...I project the twin swords.
The match should be made in an instant.
The only things in my sight are Archer and Tohsaka's back running to the church.

page24.text:
...Was it over in one blow, or was I able to hold out a few times?
The battle ends, and I look up at the sky with a limp body.
A gray color covers the sky.
It should start raining soon.
The cloudy sky is close, and the clouds block my hands like a wall.

page25.text:
"...Tohsaka, please, be safe..."
My body is burning.
I hear the faint sound of flames from the church.

page26.text:
"...Haah, agh."
The sun is too far away from my powerlessly extended hand.
That sky was as if I went back in time to ten years ago.
